messages.content: Change the settings of my air conditioner. Set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22 degrees Celsius. Enable the power save mode and set the high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now? For everything else

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to change settings of their air conditioner. They want to set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22°C. Enable power save mode and set high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now. For everything else... The phrase "For everything else" likely means keep other settings unchanged or use defaults? The user didn't specify anything about other fields. So we need to send a command with the specified fields: airConJobMode: "COOL", targetTemperature: 22, powerSaveEnabled: true, windStrength: "HIGH". Also schedule start: relativeHourToStart: 1, relativeMinuteToStart: 30. We don't set relativeHourToStop or relativeMinuteToStop (null). Also we don't set airConOperationMode? The user didn't mention turning on/off. But they said "Set it to cool mode" which implies turning on? Actually airConJobMode indicates the job mode like AIR_CLEAN, COOL, AIR_DRY. That might be separate from operation mode. The operation mode indicates whether AC is powered on or off. The user didn't mention powering on or off. But maybe setting job mode to COOL automatically powers on? Not sure. But we can set airConOperationMode to "POWER_ON" to ensure it's on. The user didn't mention enabling monitoring or air clean operation mode. So we leave them as defaults or unspecified. The function expects a body dictionary with optional keys. We can include only those we want to set. The function signature shows all keys optional. So we can pass only the ones we want.

We need to call the function ThinQ_Connect with body: {airConJobMode: "COOL", targetTemperature: 22, powerSaveEnabled: true, windStrength: "HIGH", relativeHourToStart: 1, relativeMinuteToStart: 30}. Possibly also set airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON"? The user didn't explicitly say turn on but "Set it to cool mode" might imply turning on. But we can set airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" to be safe. The user didn't mention air quality sensor monitoring or air clean operation mode. So we leave them out.

Thus we call the function.
